# Make the Formal Object Observable

Take a mathematical definition and build something that lets you *watch it behave*. Not a write-up
with worked examples — a program with a slider, a stepper, or a failure simulation. The repository
states this as its own organising thread:

> "The thread running through all six: take a formal object (a cut, a modulus, a set, a recursion, a
> graph, an information system) and make its behaviour **observable**."
> — Discrete-Mathematics-Laboratories/README.md, 2026-07-10

The verb is *observable*, not *illustrated*. The distinction is that the reader supplies the input.

## Six instances, one per lab

| Formal object | What you can watch |
|---|---|
| A cut | the best cut value climbing across ten random restarts — [[max-cut-and-local-search]] |
| A modulus | Fermat's attack collapsing as `\|p−q\|` shrinks — [[rsa-and-integer-factorization]] |
| A set | χ-sums, truth tables and inclusion–exclusion agreeing — [[characteristic-functions]] |
| A recursion | the call counter exploding while the value barely moves — [[ackermann-and-primitive-recursion]] |
| A graph | nodes failing one by one until the network splits — [[graph-connectivity-and-resilience]] |
| An information system | a query and its result rendered side by side — [[pawlak-information-system]] |

## The recurring mechanics

- **A control, not a constant.** [[matplotlib]] `Slider` widgets over `m`/`n`; Colab `#@param` form
  fields; a browser panel of lenses. The parameter that carries the concept is the one exposed.
- **Show the cost beside the answer.** A recursive-call counter, a `2^127` search space quoted next
  to a ten-restart heuristic, live graph metrics — the price of the computation is part of the
  observation.
- **Steps, not results.** BFS and DFS render as replayable step-frames rather than a final ordering.
- **Failure as an interaction.** Q-HYDRO's stackable node failures make connectivity theory something
  you break rather than read.
- **Scales chosen so something is visible.** `LogNorm` heatmaps, log-space evaluation via `lgamma` —
  a linear axis on Ackermann values shows one hot cell and nothing else.

## Why it is a pattern and not a preference

Because the same instinct survives outside the maths course. [[course-as-runnable-study-tool]] is
this pattern applied to exam revision across four other repositories; the deliverables are
double-click HTML for the same reason — [[offline-first-static-deliverable]]. The cost is real:
[[discrete-mathematics-laboratories]] has essentially no automated tests, because effort went into
making behaviour visible to a human rather than assertable by a runner. Observability substituted for
verification.
